messages.author: 8c7c2d5abf37c10c
messages.subject: Knot selection
parts:
How does inla package select knots? I would like to do a smoothing procedure but have control over where the knots are placed. Does inla function allow the user to pass a vector of e.g. where to place the knots or the number of knots needed?

tim

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Knot selection
parts:
On Thu, 2012-10-04 at 03:52 -0700, tim wrote:
> How does inla package select knots? I would like to do a smoothing
> procedure but have control over where the knots are placed. Does inla
> function allow the user to pass a vector of e.g. where to place the
> knots or the number of knots needed?
>
>
> tim

the key argument is 'values', which by default is equal to the (sorted
and uniq'ed) covariates, but it does not have to be. also, the
locations of the knots for the RW models is not that critical, as long
as there are 'enough', as the model adjusting for that in a consistent
way.

Here is a small example showing this:

n = 100
## observation locations
x = runif(n, min = 0, max = n)
## extra knots
xx = 1:n

y = sin(x/10) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.001)
## these are 'knots' in the model
values = sort(c(x, xx))
formula = y ~ 1 + f(x, model="rw2", values = values)
r = inla(formula, data = list(y=y, x=x, values=values))
plot(r$summary.random$x$ID, r$summary.random$x$mean)

Thanks a lot for the timely response. Following the example that you have posted, I can gather that a user can define more knots than there are data points i.e for example 2 knots for every data point. However, I am using inla to smooth data from a contact data matrix over different age classes. I would like to define knots which are less than my data points. i.e. I have 85 age classes but I want to define about 10 knots. The reason for this is because I know where I expect sudden changes in the contact rates and that is the place I want to put the knots. Is this possible? I hope that my question makes sense.

regards,
Tim

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Knot selection
parts:
On Thu, 2012-10-04 at 06:19 -0700, tim wrote:
> Thanks a lot for the timely response. Following the example that you
> have posted, I can gather that a user can define more knots than there
> are data points i.e for example 2 knots for every data point. However,
> I am using inla to smooth data from a contact data matrix over
> different age classes. I would like to define knots which are less
> than my data points. i.e. I have 85 age classes but I want to define
> about 10 knots. The reason for this is because I know where I expect
> sudden changes in the contact rates and that is the place I want to
> put the knots. Is this possible? I hope that my question makes sense.

there are two ways out (if you really need it).

1. you have to do it yourself using the 'A'-matrix; see the FAQ. you
must write the spline as \sum b_k(x) w_k, for weights w_k and basis
functions b_k, and then make the linear predictor {w_k} and then create
the basis functions b_k(x_i) in the A-matrix. its somewhat
complicated... I have an example around, but didn't find it
immediately, but I can recreate one, if you really needs it...

2. if you just want to reduce the number of nots, then you can use

f(inla.group(x), model="rw2")

say, where inla.group(x), reduce the number of different values in 'x'
and group them around typical values, like

> inla.group(1:10, n=3)
[1] 2.0 2.0 2.0 5.5 5.5 5.5 5.5 9.0 9.0 9.0


and this will reduce the dimension of the model, without to much loss.
there is an argument 'n' in inla.group to control the number of groups.


let us know if this does not solve your problem.

(if you use RW models then dimension 85 is not large, so maybe you can
just use all? )

H
